solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In dire cesspit, break needed!

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters across the words dire cesspit

explanation.surface: A shout that a filthy cesspit urgently needs a pause in the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or interval in proceedings, such as a parliamentary holiday, is a synonym for a break.

clue.text: Put limit on devious trickster when thousand goes missing

indicators.note: devious means the remaining letters are twisted into a new order
goes missing means the letter for thousand is taken out of trickster

parts.note: K is short for kilo, a thousand

explanation.surface: A cunning con man is curbed once a large sum disappears.
explanation.walkthrough: TRICKSTER without K leaves TRICSTER, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine or curb something is to set a limit on it, a synonym.

clue.text: Vehicle noise upsetting the French cleric

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a din is a loud noise

indicators.note: in a down answer upsetting turns the piece upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: la is French for the

explanation.surface: A churchman bothered by the racket of a passing car.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior prelate of the Roman Catholic Church, so a kind of cleric.

clue.text: Closed up after quiet drink

indicators.note: after places the turned piece behind the letters for quiet

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the piece reads from the bottom upward, so backwards

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed

explanation.surface: A bar shut after a peaceful drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A door pushed 'to' is closed; 'up' turns it in this down light, and 'after' sets it behind the call for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of spirits, downed in one, is a drink.

clue.text: Dish served by firm (American) twice over

indicators.note: twice over says the pair of pieces just built is written down two times in a row

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A dish brought out by an American company, served up two times.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African dish of steamed semolina grains, so an example of a dish.

clue.text: Unbearably intense giver mixed with new poor

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of giver, new and poor are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A donor mingling with the destitute finds it all too much.
explanation.definitionFit: So strong it overwhelms the senses, as with a smell, so too intense to bear.

clue.text: Ephemeral, this love disheartened daughter terribly

indicators.note: terribly says the gathered letters are badly jumbled into a new order
disheartened means the word daughter loses its middle, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A fleeting romance leaves a daughter terribly downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' strips DAUGHTER to DR, which joins THIS LOVE in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting only a brief time, so transient, which is a synonym for ephemeral.

clue.text: Month needed by worker to produce instrument

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October, a month
a worker ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: A month's labour is needed to make a device.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigational device for measuring angles, using an eighth of a circle, is an instrument.

clue.text: Councillor's noticed outside shelter

indicators.note: outside means the word for noticed goes round the abbreviation for councillor

parts.note: seen means noticed
Cllr or CR is an abbreviation for councillor; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A local politician is spotted outside a shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen hides or protects, so it serves as a shelter or shield.

clue.text: Address child about school period head left

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, here the child wrapping the shortened school period

parts.note: a son is a child

indicators.note: head left means the first letter of the school period is dropped

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year

explanation.surface: A parent lecturing a child after the headteacher has gone for the term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head left' takes T from TERM, leaving ERM, which SON goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech or talk, especially a preacher's, is an address in the noun sense.

clue.text: Extremely reliable one carrying bags for media person

indicators.note: Extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last, of the word reliable

parts.note: a porter carries luggage at a hotel or station

explanation.surface: A dependable bag-carrier turns out to be working for the press.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who gathers news for a paper or broadcaster is a person working in the media.

clue.text: Domestic worker at end of month has bonus due? Ludicrous!

indicators.note: at end of picks the final letter of the word month
Ludicrous says the letters of has bonus due are absurdly rearranged

explanation.surface: A homemaker expecting a bonus at the end of the month is told that is absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who stays home doing housework and childcare, so a domestic worker.

clue.text: Right to support attack

parts.note: aid means help or support

explanation.surface: A claim that one has the right to back an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden assault or incursion on a place is an attack, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Take part in contest at French resort with one lacking ability

parts.note: to compete is to take part in a contest

indicators.note: lacking means the resort name loses the letter that stands for one

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone entering a contest in a French resort with a partner who has no skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Capability or skill to do something properly is a synonym for ability.

clue.text: Pursuing idea, state has time for new settlement

indicators.note: Pursuing puts the state piece behind the word for idea, chasing it

parts.note: a plan is an idea

indicators.note: has time for new means a letter for time replaces the letter for new

parts.note: a nation is a state

explanation.surface: A government follows through on an idea for a new colony.
explanation.walkthrough: NATION 'has time for new': its first N becomes T, giving TATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony planted overseas was historically a settlement, as in the Ulster Plantation.

clue.text: Plough in-law crashes disastrously

indicators.note: disastrously says the letters of in-law crashes are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A relative by marriage has a terrible car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The Plough is the British name for the star pattern also called the Big Dipper; CHARLES'S WAIN is its old name.
explanation.definitionFit: The star grouping in Ursa Major known as the Plough has the traditional alternative name of Charles's Wain.

clue.text: Accomplished story, famous — nothing lacking

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: lacking means the zero letter is removed from the word for famous

parts.note: noted means famous
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A celebrated story with nothing missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifted and skilled, so accomplished as an adjective meaning able.

clue.text: Education employee, unusually curt, to look sneeringly around

indicators.note: around means the word for looking sneeringly is wrapped round the jumbled letters

parts.note: to leer is to look slyly or sneeringly

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of curt are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A rude teacher sneers at those around them.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rude lecturer, but 'curt' is only fodder: 'unusually' scrambles it, and 'around' wraps the sneering look about the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A university teacher giving lectures is employed in education.

clue.text: Predictable outcome from this here once, oars involved

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters of here once and oars are tangled up together into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowing race where the result was obvious from this spot long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest with only one plausible winner, so its result is a foregone conclusion.

clue.text: British set up hospital project ultimately full of promise

parts.note: to rig is to set up, as with equipment or a fix
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word project

explanation.surface: Britain launches a hospital scheme that looks hopeful in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright future is a promising one, so the word means showing promise.

clue.text: He allots animal cherished by senior

indicators.note: cherished by means the animal is held inside, embraced by the abbreviation for senior

parts.note: a hare is an animal

explanation.surface: An elderly man fond of a pet rabbit hands out portions.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who divides things out among others gives each a portion, so he allots.

clue.text: Tries again at home — good at practice?

parts.note: to rehear a case is to try it again in court
in means at home

explanation.surface: A court retrying a case from home, and wondering whether that counts as good practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries again' is legal: a court that rehears a case tries it a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Going through a performance before the real thing means one is busy practising it.

clue.text: Jaunty Pierrot regularly missing

indicators.note: regularly missing means every other letter of Pierrot is left out, keeping the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: A cheerful clown who keeps failing to show up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively, cheeky and sprightly in manner, so a close synonym for jaunty.

clue.text: Genuine cessation of conflict, its start forgotten

indicators.note: its start forgotten means the first letter of cessation, a C, is dropped from the word for a halt in fighting

parts.note: a truce is a cessation of conflict

explanation.surface: A real ceasefire, though no one remembers how it began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its start' is the C that begins 'cessation'; dropping it from TRUCE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Real or authentic, so a direct synonym for genuine.

clue.text: Malinger criminally at very early stage

indicators.note: criminally says the letters of Malinger are wrongly treated and rearranged

explanation.surface: Faking illness right from the start is an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing something just beginning to develop, like a seed sprouting, which is an embryonic phase.

clue.text: Speaker some parrot, a Rotarian from the east

indicators.note: from the east means the letters are read right to left, as in an across answer read backwards
some means only part of the run of letters in parrot, a Rotarian is taken

explanation.surface: Someone who repeats what a club member from the east says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ROTARO from parROT A ROtarian; 'from the east' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A person giving a speech or public address is a speaker, a synonym.

clue.text: Lament changes made by trendy host (no Saint!)

indicators.note: changes says the gathered letters are rearranged into a new order
no means the letters for saint are taken out of host

explanation.surface: A fashionable party-giver alters a song of mourning, and is no saint about it.
explanation.walkthrough: HOST without ST leaves HO, which joins TRENDY in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A song or poem of mourning for the dead is a lament, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Ancillary vehicle easily crushed

definitions.meaning: a small boat or a coal wagon serving a larger ship or locomotive
soft, delicate, readily bruised, as of meat or fruit

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a supply boat or coal truck attending a bigger vessel, and soft or delicate.
